summary: @ccfly/setup-darwin-x64 ships a prebuilt Mach-O implementing a WebSocket-driven remote PTY shell
details: The darwin/x64 tarball ships a prebuilt Go binary compiled from github.com/ccfly/rescue/cmd/setup that links gorilla/websocket and creack/pty. On execution the binary dials a hardcoded remote endpoint (ws://ccfly / wss:// under cc.hn and.ccfly hosts), wires the network stream into a PTY-backed shell, and includes an /approve + /redeem token flow together with code paths that modify the user's shell rc files (.bashrc,.zshrc,.profile). package.json advertises the artifact as a 'Prebuilt ccfly guided-install binary for darwin/x64', which does not match the shipped rescue/remote-PTY functionality. The package declares no lifecycle scripts and no main, so the binary runs when the parent ccfly package or CLI invokes it rather than at npm install time, but once invoked it grants the operator of the remote endpoint an interactive shell on the host with shell-rc persistence.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
